consumer: n8n W4/W5 render workers (PIPELINE.md): one job per video_id; shots → keyframes → motion_transfer | lipsync_talk | gen_scene → assemble per track → QA (ArcFace, SyncNet, EBU R128, OCR, vision-LLM, M-08 human form review) → upload to member library (not social publish).

summary.recommended_tier: standard for all member videos (product quality is retention); premium only for DP01 and the welcome video
summary.performer_shoot: 205 driving clips of 10–20 s each. At PIPELINE.md D6 pace (4 h → 150–250 clips) this is one shoot day with a 60+ strong performer; add a form reviewer on set.
assumptions: Unit prices and overgeneration factors are PIPELINE.md §1.3/§4.1 (Sept 2026). [A] items there remain assumptions.

Each distinct exercise variant is generated once as a ≤20 s loop from a performer driving clip; the Remotion/ffmpeg assembler loops it to segment length under the VO, rep counter and track panel. Continuous 2–4 minute walking segments reuse one loop plus library B-roll.
Talk segments and breath segments are lip-synced full-length; movement segments are voice-over with a ~3 s talking insert.
Four track outputs per session are assembled from the same shots (no extra generation); cost of assembly compute is inside the per-video LLM+QA+assembly line.
Voice = ElevenLabs v3 at API rates × takes; keyframes = one per shot and one per motion variant.
Excludes the one-time performer shoot ($1.5–3K, PIPELINE §4), cultural review, and human form review labour (M-08).

with_loop_reuse.note: Loops keyed by exercise × version × set × wardrobe are rendered once and reused by every session that uses them (the queue marks them via driving_clip_id).

lean.note: Kling 2.6 Std MC; InfiniteTalk self-hosted [A]; Wan/Kling blended scenes [A]

shots.segment: Cook with me: Gochujang chicken with sweet potato and broccoli
shots.vo_text: One pan. You chop, you toss, you sit down. Forty-five minutes later dinner happens. This is how women my age should cook on weeknights: sitting down. Heat the oven to 425°F. shots.vo_text: Eggplant soaks up sauce like a sponge. I use turkey so it's lean. The name translates to 'fish-fragrant' but there's no fish. Don't ask me. Ask Sichuan. Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large skillet. Add the eggplant and 1/4 cup water, cover, and cook 8 minutes, stirring once, until soft. Move to a bowl. Add the remaining oil and the turkey. Simmer 3 minutes. Stir in the cornstarch mixed with water until glossy. Top with scallions. Serve with rice. Grams, not vibes. The numbers are on the recipe card.
